rules.summary: Oklahoma law lists a free forensic medical examination among the rights of a sexual assault victim.
rules.quote: The right to a free forensic medical examination

rules.summary: The exam fund pays whether or not the survivor has health insurance, and the survivor does not have to give insurance or employment information or file with a private insurer.
rules.quote: The payment of a sexual assault examination will be made, regardless of whether the victim is medically insured. (b) In order to provide anonymity to the sexual assault victim and maintain confidentiality, any victim who has obtained a forensic sexual assault examination, will not be required to provide information to the Board relative to employment or insurance; and, shall not be required to file a claim with any private insurance company for the payment of a forensic sexual assault examination.

params.payer: Sexual Assault Examination Fund, administered by the Crime Victims Compensation Board (Oklahoma District Attorneys Council)

rules.summary: The Crime Victims Compensation Board pays for the sexual assault forensic exam and related medications out of the Sexual Assault Examination Fund.
rules.quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Board is authorized to pay for this examination and the medications directed by the qualified licensed health care professional upon application submitted by the victim of a sexual assault.

rules.summary: The exam fund pays at most $800 for a sexual assault examination.
rules.quote: in no event shall the Crime Victims Compensation Board pay an amount to exceed: 1. Eight Hundred Dollars ($800.00) for a sexual assault examination

rules.summary: The exam fund pays at most $100 for medications related to the sexual assault that the health care professional directs.
rules.quote: One Hundred Dollars ($100.00) for medications which are related to the sexual assault and directed and deemed necessary by the health care professional

params.payer: Sexual Assault Examination Fund, paid directly to the service provider

rules.summary: For sexual assaults on or after November 1, 2023, up to $800 can be paid straight to the exam providers for exam and facility fees.
rules.quote: For sexual assaults occurring on or after November 1, 2023, the law allows payment of up to $800 which may be paid directly to the service provider(s) for expenses incurred for the forensic examination (such as an examination fee or a facility fee).
rules.pinpoint: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

rules.summary: Total compensation for one victim is capped at $25,000. After that, the Board may add up to $25,000 more only for the victim's lost wages or a dependent's loss of support.
rules.quote: Compensation payable to a victim and to all other claimants sustaining economic loss because of injury to or death of that victim may not exceed Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00) in the aggregate. The Board may, after approval of an initial award of Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00), grant an additional sum not to exceed Twenty-five Thousand Dollars ($25,000.00), specifically for loss of wages for the victim or loss of support for dependents of a deceased victim, provided there is verifiable economic loss after deducting payments from other sources.

rules.summary: Outpatient counseling for the victim is capped at $3,000 in total. The same subsection lets the Board waive this limit in extreme cases.
rules.quote: A total not to exceed Three Thousand Dollars ($3,000.00) may be awarded for individual counseling sessions for victims of criminally injurious conduct.

rules.summary: Inpatient mental health treatment is reviewed case by case and may be paid up to $20,000.
rules.quote: Inpatient mental health treatment will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis and may be compensated, at the discretion of the Board, in an amount not to exceed Twenty Thousand Dollars ($20,000.00).

rules.summary: Lost income of a caregiver who missed work to care for the injured victim is capped at $3,000. This cap is for the caregiver, not the victim's own lost wages.
rules.quote: Loss of income of a caregiver shall not exceed Three Thousand Dollars ($3,000.00).

rules.summary: Funeral, cremation, or burial expenses are capped at $7,500.
rules.quote: Reasonable funeral, cremation or burial expenses shall not exceed Seven Thousand Five Hundred Dollars ($7,500.00).

rules.summary: Crime scene cleanup is capped at $2,000.
rules.quote: Reasonable costs associated with crime scene cleanup shall not exceed Two Thousand Dollars ($2,000.00).

rules.summary: Medical services are covered at up to 80% of the cost of the service.
rules.quote: Awards for all medical services shall not exceed eighty percent (80%) of the total cost of the service less any other reduction for contributory conduct, as determined by the Board.

rules.summary: A medical, dental, or psychological provider that accepts the program's payment must treat it as payment in full and cannot bill the claimant for the rest of those services.
rules.quote: Any medical provider that receives payment from the Crime Victims Compensation Revolving Fund for medical, dental or psychological services, or any provider that supplies equipment pursuant to an award under the Oklahoma Crime Victims Compensation Act shall, as a condition of the receipt of such payment, accept such payment as discharging in full any and all obligations of the claimant to pay, reimburse or compensate the provider

rules.summary: If the survivor already paid a medical bill, the program reimburses the out-of-pocket amount, less any conduct reduction.
rules.quote: In the event the claimant has paid for a medical service, the claimant will be reimbursed for the out-of-pocket loss, less any reductions for contributory conduct, as determined by the Board.

rules.summary: The Board may pay for the victim's lost income from work (work loss).
rules.quote: The Crime Victims Compensation Board may compensate for work loss, replacement services loss, dependent

rules.summary: Outpatient counseling is covered when it focuses on the crime and the counselor is a qualified mental health provider.
rules.quote: Outpatient counseling expenses for a victim of criminally injurious conduct may be considered by the Board provided the counseling is focused on the crime and the counselor is a qualified mental health care provider.

rules.summary: The program lists mileage to the victim's medical, dental, and counseling appointments as a covered expense.
rules.quote: Mileage reimbursement for medical, dental, and counseling appointments for the victim

rules.summary: The program lists dental care and prescriptions among covered expenses.
rules.quote: Medical, dental, and prescriptions

params.item: personal property and pain and suffering

rules.summary: Personal property (for example a damaged or stolen phone) and pain and suffering are not reimbursed.
rules.quote: Pain and suffering and personal property are NOT allowable expenses under the Crime Victims Compensation Act

params.extension: The Board may extend the filing period for good cause or in all cases of sexual assault; for adult sexual assault it may count from the date the evidence kit was tested.

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within 30 months after the injury. The sexual assault and good-cause extensions are in the next rule.
rules.quote: Unless the claim has been filed with the Crime Victims Compensation Board within thirty (30) months after the injury or death upon which the claim is based.

params.extension: kit-tested date may be used for adult sexual assault; Board may extend for good cause or in all sexual assault cases

rules.summary: For an adult (18 or older) sexual assault, the Board may measure timeliness from the date the evidence kit was tested, and it may extend the filing period for good cause or in any sexual assault case.
rules.quote: In cases involving sexual assault of an adult eighteen (18) years of age or older, the Board may use the date the sexual assault forensic evidence kit was tested when establishing whether the claim was timely filed. The Board may, at its discretion, extend the filing period beyond one (1) year upon a showing of good cause or in all cases of sexual assault

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to police within 72 hours, but a sexual assault survivor can instead meet this by having a forensic medical exam within 120 hours, and the Board can excuse either for good cause.
rules.quote: such conduct was reported to a law enforcement officer within seventy-two (72) hours after its occurrence, b. in the case of sexual assault, the victim undergoes a forensic medical examination within one hundred twenty (120) hours after its occurrence, or c. the Board finds there was good cause for the failure to report the crime or obtain a forensic medical examination within the time specified in subparagraph a or b of this paragraph.

rules.summary: A sexual assault survivor who has a forensic medical exam within 120 hours is treated as having fully cooperated with law enforcement. This is the cooperation rule; the report rule itself is OK-RPT-1.
rules.quote: Victims of sexual assault who undergo a forensic medical examination within one hundred twenty (120) hours after the sexual assault shall be found to have fully cooperated.

rules.summary: Awards are reduced by anything insurance or other collateral sources pay for the same loss.
rules.quote: Compensation otherwise payable to a claimant shall be diminished to the extent: 1. That the economic loss is recouped from collateral sources

rules.summary: The Board may reduce an award by the degree of responsibility it attributes to the victim. Tend shows this only as information.
rules.quote: Of the degree of responsibility for the cause of the injury or death attributable to the victim as determined by the Board.

rules.summary: If the claimant would face financial hardship otherwise, the Board can pay an advance that comes out of the final award.
rules.quote: If the Board determines that the claimant will suffer financial hardship unless an advance award is made, an amount may be paid to the claimant and shall be deducted from the final award

rules.summary: Victims who suffered physical or psychological harm or death from a violent crime can qualify.
rules.quote: A primary requirement is that the crime be one in which the victim suffered physical or psychological harm or death as a result of a violent crime.

params.rule: Crimes in Oklahoma (any victim), or crimes against Oklahoma residents in a state without an eligible VOCA compensation program.

rules.summary: The crime must have happened in Oklahoma, or be against an Oklahoma resident in a state without an eligible compensation program.
rules.quote: a misdemeanor or felony which occurs or is attempted in this state, or against a resident of this state in a state that does not have an eligible crime victims compensation program

rules.summary: For the exam fund, Medicaid or another federally funded program counts as a collateral source, so the fund pays only after that program denies the exam.
rules.quote: For sexual assault exams performed on adults and children, Medicaid or any other federally funded program is considered a collateral source and payment will not be made unless the denial of benefits is provided.

params.payer: Sexual Assault Examination Fund; examiner and facility fees share the $800 limit pro rata

rules.summary: Only charges directly tied to the forensic exam are paid, and when the examiner fee and the facility fee together exceed $800 the fund splits the $800 between the providers by percentage.
rules.quote: Any charges not directly related to the forensic exam are not compensable. In cases where there is both an examiner fee and a facility fee exceeding $800, we prorate, allowing a percentage to each provider.
rules.pinpoint: DAC Sexual Assault Examination Fund page

rules.summary: For the exam fund and the sexual assault rights notice, sexual assault means rape, rape by instrumentation, or forcible sodomy as defined in the criminal code.
rules.quote: rape, or rape by instrumentation, as defined in Sections 1111 , 1111.1 and 1114 of this title, or b. forcible sodomy, as defined in Section 888 of this title

rules.summary: Apply online through the OCVC online application portal.
rules.quote: Use our online application to apply for compensation benefits.

rules.quote: Medical, dental, and counseling expenses that the victim is out-of-pocket will be reimbursed at 100%, provided there is documentation of payment and no collateral sources exist.

rules.quote: A police report is requested, along with any other forms and reports that may be needed to determine out-of-pocket expenses.

coverage.notes: No dollar minimum loss was found; program pages only say there must be economic loss. Relocation, security, and temporary housing are not listed as allowable expenses in 21 O.S. 142.3 or on the program pages, and no cap for the victim's own lost wages was found beyond the overall cap. Medical services are limited to 80% of cost rather than a dollar cap. No statute was found that expressly bars a provider from billing the survivor for exam charges above the $800 fund limit.

researcher_notes: Statutes (OSCN, 21 O.S. as amended by SB 420, eff. Nov 1, 2023) win over program pages. Conflicts: the DAC page and the 2019 claim form say the total cap is $20,000 ($40,000 with the wage add-on) and the filing deadline is one year; current 142.13(B) says $25,000 ($50,000) and 142.10(A)(1) says thirty months. The OCVC eligibility page says caregiver work loss is $2,000 but 142.13(A) and (K) say $3,000. 142.10(A)(1) still has a leftover phrase about extending 'beyond one (1) year' next to the new 30-month period. The Board may grant up to $25,000 beyond the base cap for wages or loss of support, with a hard ceiling of $50,000 under 142.13(B). The application PDF is the 2019 form and predates the 2023 changes; the online claim at ocvcapp.okvictimscomp.com is the primary route. OAC 185:10-1-4 still says one year and was not used. The filing_deadline rule uses a 'months' param because the schema only lists years or days. Exam: OAC 185:15-1-6(d) treats Medicaid or other federal programs as a collateral source that must deny first; private insurance is optional for the survivor and any insurance payment goes back to the fund (185:15-1-6(c)). Providers must stop debt collection once notified of a pending claim (21 O.S. 142.9(H)). Reviewer: the OCVC home page still says a claim should be filed within one year, and the eligibility page says 'within one (30) months'; the statute's 30 months controls. 142.3 on OSCN lists amendments only through 2007 even though its text mentions vehicle impound fees, so its history note may be incomplete. Vehicle impound fees are capped at $750 (142.13(L)) and homicide family crisis counseling at $3,000 (142.13(G)); neither was added as a rule because neither applies to a living sexual assault survivor. The DAC exam page says the $800 limit applies to assaults on or after November 1, 2023, so older assaults may fall under an earlier, lower limit that was not researched. How to file: the online portal (ocvcapp.okvictimscomp.com) is the main route; its page says written applications go by mail or fax, while the 2019 claim form says to print, sign, and then fax, email, or mail it, so email comes only from the form. The current printable application is still the June 2019 claim form (OK-S12), which the portal links; it is a flat PDF with no fillable fields (pypdf found 0), and the DAC page still links older 2016/2017 forms that were not used. No in-person filing method is stated. The police report is requested by the DA's Victim-Witness Coordinator, not attached by the survivor. Processing times come from program pages, not statute: the FAQ says 4 to 12 months overall, the DAC page says claims are docketed within 30 days of full documentation and paid within three weeks of approval.
